description: Every book from AI Engineer Press, with its chapters, their URLs and status, and the explainer video for each chapter that has one.

chapters.title: The Shift: From Assistant to Delegate
chapters.promise: Why the important transition is not better chat UX, but reliable delegated work.

chapters.title: Taste Still Matters When Code Gets Cheap
chapters.promise: Why fundamentals, judgment, craft, and constraint become more valuable.

chapters.title: Harnesses, Specs, and Codebases Agents Can Actually Use
chapters.promise: How prepared environments make coding agents useful without accepting slop.

chapters.title: Evals Are the Control System
chapters.promise: Why production trust comes from measurement loops, not vibes.

chapters.title: Context Is Infrastructure
chapters.promise: Retrieval, memory, and knowledge layers as first-class system design.

chapters.title: Runtimes, State, and the Human Control Plane
chapters.promise: Durable agents, replay vs snapshot, and why autonomy needs architecture.

chapters.title: Security, Identity, and High-Stakes Trust
chapters.promise: Why delegated authority needs boundaries, audit trails, and real controls.

chapters.title: Realtime, Voice, and the Cost of Being Interruptible
chapters.promise: What voice, latency, and turn-taking reveal about production AI.

chapters.title: The AI-Native Organization
chapters.promise: How teams and incentives change when AI becomes part of the workforce.

chapters.title: What Endures
chapters.promise: The principles that survive tool churn: context, evals, control, and taste.

books.title: The Model Layer & The Long Tail
books.subtitle: Training, Inference, and the Domains Beyond Text
books.blurb: An early, source-anchored draft on how AI engineering is reshaping training, inference, and the long tail of domains beyond text.

chapters.title: Training and the Turn to RL
chapters.promise: Why the center of gravity in model-building moved from pre-training to post-training — and reinforcement learning above all.

chapters.title: Inference Economics
chapters.promise: Why serving a model, not training it, is where the cost, the latency, and most AI engineering careers actually live.

chapters.title: Building Frontier Models
chapters.promise: Why building a frontier model became its own engineering culture, and why the frontier is now crowded rather than a two-lab race.

chapters.title: Beyond Text: Models for Speech, Media, Perception, and Action
chapters.promise: How speech, media, recommendation, driving, and embodiment models are all converging on the same LLM-shaped design.

chapters.title: Robotics and the Physical World
chapters.promise: Why robotics is not "agents plus a body" — the physical world adds constraints the standard harness never has to handle.

chapters.title: Regulated and High-Stakes Domains
chapters.promise: Why finance, legal, insurance, and medicine need a different engineering posture, not just a smarter general model.

chapters.title: Creative, Education, and Games
chapters.promise: Why creative, educational, and game applications keep the model in a narrow lane while structured systems hold the ground truth.

chapters.title: What the Edges Teach
chapters.promise: What the model layer and the long tail say together: capability consolidates, accountability does not, and the constraints were never compensation for a weak model.

books.title: The Shape of the Work
books.subtitle: When Writing the Code Stops Being the Constraint
books.blurb: Spec-driven development and the software factory: what happens to the lifecycle when writing the code stops being the constraint.
books.measure: 12 of 12 chapters · 133 talks classified · spec published

chapters.title: The Bottleneck Moved
chapters.promise: Why "code generation was never the bottleneck" reframes the whole lifecycle — and why the feeling of going faster is not evidence that you are.

chapters.title: Intent Before Specification
chapters.promise: What has to be settled before any document helps — and why the instinct to specify first fails on capabilities nobody has mapped yet.

chapters.title: What a Specification Is For
chapters.promise: Code is a lossy projection of the reasoning that produced it. A specification is the surface you argue on before that reasoning is lost.

chapters.title: Decomposition and the Plan
chapters.promise: Why the size of a planned step is a context constraint rather than a matter of taste, and why a bad line in a plan costs a hundred bad lines of code.

chapters.title: Execution Under a Spec
chapters.promise: A specification binds through exactly two mechanisms — what the agent can reach, and what gets checked afterwards. Everything else is advisory.

chapters.title: The Independence Problem
chapters.promise: A judge that nearly doubled a benchmark score, and why the most dangerous gate in your pipeline is the one you wrote yourself.

chapters.title: Gates That Can Actually Fail
chapters.promise: Gates die two ways: crying wolf, or never objecting. The second is silent, gets praised, and is far more dangerous.

chapters.title: Shipping, and the Gap Between Merged and Live
chapters.promise: Thirty consecutive commits that deployed nothing while every indicator said success — and why an absence produces no artifact.

chapters.title: Brownfield and Spec Rot
chapters.promise: When the system is too large to hold in view, every slice is locally correct and the whole drifts. Three different decays hide under one phrase.

chapters.title: The Review Wall
chapters.promise: Lines of code up 2,450%. Commits up 240%. Releases up 30%. The gap is inventory, and "human in the loop" is where it gets relabelled as control.

chapters.title: The Factory and Its Discontents
chapters.promise: A factory makes the same thing repeatedly. Software never makes the same thing twice — which is why the metaphor works for some work and strains everywhere else.

chapters.title: How Much Process, and How Far Out of the Loop
chapters.promise: Two measured rounds where ceremony cost a third more tokens for an identical scorecard — and the one result no scorecard could see.
